extracted.intended_audience: writers and company staff responsible for proposing, preparing, submitting, or disputing writing credits on theatrical motion pictures (WGA signatory productions)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural checklist for preparing and submitting Notices of Tentative Writing Credits (NTWCs), obtaining waivers, complying with on-screen placement, and assembling materials for credit arbitrations for theatrical motion pictures under the WGA/MBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTWC must be submitted to the Guild and to all participating writers as soon as practicable following completion of principal photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NTWC sets the mechanism for determination of credits and must be sent promptly after principal photography is complete (TSA, ¶11). It advises writers of proposed credit and deadline to protest or elect a pseudonym.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTWC recipients and listing of participating writers
rubrics_metrics.description: List the names and addresses of all participating writers at the top of the NTWC and send the NTWC to the Guild and all participating writers (unless contract directs delivery to an agent/designated representative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must list all participating writers even if they are not proposed for credit. A 'participating writer' includes any writer who participated in the screenplay, was employed by the Company on the story/screenplay, or a 'professional writer' who sold/licensed literary material under the MBA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verified delivery methods for NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: The NTWC must be sent via Certified Mail/Return Receipt Requested, messenger, or other independently verifiable means; e-mail is not considered independently verifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use methods that provide proof of delivery (TSA, ¶¶2, 12 and 17).

rubrics_metrics.name: NTWC must list project title and production executives
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the title of the motion picture and the names of all production executives (director, producers, executive producers, co-producers, associate producers, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate on the NTWC if a participating writer will also be credited as a production executive; give notice before writing credits are determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed on-screen writing credit format
rubrics_metrics.description: List the proposed on-screen writing credit including the form (e.g., 'Written by', 'Screenplay by'), not just author names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers may only be credited in the manner set forth in the MBA unless a waiver is granted. If uncertain, consult the Screen Credits Manual (SCM) or the Credits Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted/allowable writing credit types
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowable writing credits include: 'Written by,' 'Screenplay by,' 'Story by,' 'Screen Story by,' 'Adaptation by,' 'Narration Written by,' and 'Based on Characters Created by.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult SCM for appropriate form; some combined credits require waivers (see Waivers section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampersand (&) vs 'and' usage between writer names
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an ampersand ('&') between names of writers who worked as a team; use the word 'and' between names of writers who did not work as a team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction affects perceived authorship (SCM, pg. 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Source material credit on NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any on-screen source material credit (e.g., 'Based on the Novel by') on the NTWC and list all source material whether or not it will appear on screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally use 'Novel' for fiction and 'Book' for non-fiction. Source material includes prior pictures for remakes/sequels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and production credits on NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: Include on the NTWC any presentation and/or production credit to be accorded on screen and/or in advertising (e.g., 'Universal Pictures Presents' or 'A Film by').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These credits must be declared to ensure compliance with the MBA (TSA, ¶28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending final shooting script with NTWC
rubrics_metrics.description: Send a copy of the final shooting script to all participating writers, including those not proposed for credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is required (TSA, ¶11) to allow writers and the Guild to review the text on which credits are based.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper calculation of final-credit deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Properly calculate the date on which proposed credits become final absent a protest (generally twelve business days from the date the NTWC is sent; may be shortened to seven business days in a good faith emergency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If automatic arbitration provisions apply, write 'Automatic Arbitration' in place of a final date (TSA, ¶13). The 'date sent' is the actual send date, not the preparation date.

rubrics_metrics.name: NTWC signature and company contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: List the name, address, telephone number of the production company and authorized representative and ensure the NTWC is signed by the Company's authorized representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the actual date the NTWC is sent to Guild and participating writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'participating writer'
rubrics_metrics.description: A participating writer is a writer who has participated in the writing of the screenplay, a writer employed by the Company on the story and/or screenplay, or a 'professional writer' who has sold or licensed literary material subject to the MBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Article 1.B.1.b. of the MBA for the definition of 'professional writer.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration Agreement for certain team collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: A Collaboration Agreement is required when a production executive writes in collaboration as a team with a non-production executive writer and the production executive intends to claim co-authorship of the team's material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A writing services agreement employing both as a team can serve as a Collaboration Agreement (SCM, pg. 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Team waiver requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Team waivers are required for writing teams of four or more people; a 'team' is generally no more than two writers (or three in the specific Article 13.A.9 situation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers must be requested and approved in advance of services being performed. Contact Contracts Department to request team waivers (TSA, ¶4; SCM, pg. 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arbitration triggers (automatic arbitration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic credit arbitration is triggered in these situations: (1) when a production executive is proposed for writing credit and there are other non-production executive participating writers; (2) when a 'Screen Story by' credit is proposed; (3) when an 'Adaptation by' credit is proposed; (4) when three writers are proposed for 'Written by' or 'Screenplay by' credit (a team counts as a single writer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic arbitration is governed by the MBA (TSA, ¶6; SCM pp. 19–23). If triggered, indicate 'Automatic Arbitration' on the NTWC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials required for arbitration
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a protest or with an automatic arbitration, the Company must submit three copies of all literary material submitted to or acquired by the Company by all participating writers and any source material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Literary material includes beatsheets, outlines, stories, treatments, scripts, formats, etc. Also submit a transmittal letter identifying each piece by author and date. (TSA, ¶18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover page requirements on literary material
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover pages on all literary material must comply with MBA Article 37: upon commencement of pre-production, Company shall place the name of the initial writer on literary material, followed by the word 'revisions' preceding the names of subsequent writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the sample cover page form provided and follow MBA/SCM guidance to avoid disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waivers for special circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Waivers from the Guild are required for: (1) writing teams of four or more; (2) screenings prior to the Guild's final determination of writing credits for festivals or public exhibitions; and (3) combining certain credits (Written, Produced, and Directed by; Written and Produced by; Written for the Screen and Directed by).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the Contracts or Credits Department to request appropriate waivers in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen placement of writing credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing credits usually must appear on a separate card contiguous to the director's credit, with specific ordering rules for 'Screenplay by' and 'Story by' depending on main vs end-title formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main titles: if 'Screenplay by' and 'Story by' are on the same card, 'Screenplay by' must be in the top 50% of the card; if on separate cards, 'Story by' must precede 'Screenplay by'. End titles: 'Screenplay by' always precedes 'Story by' and they may appear on the same or separate cards. The writing credit must appear in the main titles if any personal names or initials appear in the main titles (TSA, ¶8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement rules for source material credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Source material credit may appear in main or end titles and should be on a separate card from the writing credit, except where the source material author is also the sole credited screenplay writer (then it may appear on the same card).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source material credit may not be placed between the 'Screenplay by' credit and the director's credit when those credits are on separate cards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of main and end titles for WGA approval
rubrics_metrics.description: You are required to submit the main and end titles for the picture to the WGA for approval before any prints are prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval ensures on-screen credits conform to MBA provisions and helps avoid penalties for non-compliance (TSA, ¶8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of publicity and advertising for WGA approval
rubrics_metrics.description: All publicity and advertising material must be submitted to the WGA for approval prior to issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures publicity/advertising conforms to MBA provisions and avoids penalties (TSA, ¶26).
